POSTS.t: How Local SEO Gets Your Business Into the Google Map Pack
POSTS.x: Three things decide who shows up in the map pack: relevance, distance and prominence. Here is how to improve the two you control.
b: When someone searches “near me”, Google shows three businesses on a map before any normal result. Those three spots get most of the calls.
Start with a complete Google Business Profile: the right primary category, every service you offer, real photos each month and accurate hours.
Then build consistent citations, and earn recent, detailed reviews. Reply to every review within a couple of days.

POSTS.t: Google Ads vs SEO: Where Should Your First Marketing Dollar Go?
POSTS.x: Ads bring leads this week, SEO compounds over months. The right answer depends on your cash flow and how competitive your market is.
b: Google Ads put you at the top of results today, but the leads stop when the budget stops.
SEO takes 3 to 6 months to build, then keeps sending leads without paying per click.
For most service businesses we start with a small, tightly tracked ads campaign while SEO builds in the background.

POSTS.t: AI Search Optimization: Getting Mentioned by ChatGPT and Google AI
POSTS.x: More customers ask AI tools for recommendations. Clear structured data and answer-ready content help these tools understand and cite you.
b: AI answer engines pull from sources they trust and content they can understand quickly.
Add structured data that describes your business, write clear answers to the questions customers ask, and keep your details consistent across the web.
Then track where you are mentioned, and improve the pages that AI tools cite.

POSTS.t: 7 Website Fixes That Turn Visitors Into Phone Calls
POSTS.x: Small changes like a visible phone number, faster pages and one clear offer per page often double enquiries.
b: Put your phone number and main call to action at the top of every page, especially on mobile.
Make pages load in under three seconds, and show reviews near the contact form.
Give each service its own page with one clear offer and one next step.

POSTS.t: What a Transparent Marketing Report Should Show You
POSTS.x: If your report is full of impressions and jargon, something is missing. Here are the numbers that actually matter.
b: A useful report starts with business results: calls, form leads, booked jobs and sales.
Then it shows the work done that month and what is planned next.
Rankings and traffic matter, but only as signals on the way to leads.

POSTS.t: Social Media for Service Businesses: A Simple Monthly Plan
POSTS.x: You don’t need to post every day. A simple monthly mix of proof, tips and offers keeps you visible without burning out.
b: Plan four types of posts: before-and-after work, quick tips, customer reviews and one clear offer.
Batch-create them once a month and schedule them.
Reply to every comment and message quickly. That is where social turns into leads.
